title: Explainable ensemble machine learning for reliable concrete compressive strength prediction: a validation and uncertainty assessment framework
task: Explainable ensemble machine learning for concrete compressive strength prediction with uncertainty quantification
key_results: Stacking ensemble achieves R²=0.9245, MAE=2.8561, RMSE=4.3892; Gradient Boosting shows highest cross-validation stability (R²=0.9244); external validation confirms reasonable generalization
comments: Rigorous validation framework with 10-fold CV and held-out test set; performance degradation on external data suggests domain shift limitations.

model_io.model: Stacking ensemble (RF, XGBoost, CatBoost, LightGBM, Gradient Boosting)
inputs: concrete mix design: water, cement, sand, coarse aggregate, curing age

hypotheses.hypothesis: Ensemble learning captures nonlinear strength relationships better than individual models and provides reliable predictions under similar conditions
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: stacking ensemble R²=0.9245 on test set; external validation shows reasonable generalization with caveats

title: Development and benchmark validation of PubChat for PubMed-grounded multilingual biomedical literature retrieval
task: Development and benchmark validation of PubChat: PubMed-grounded multilingual biomedical literature retrieval
key_results: PubChat produces zero fabricated citations in benchmark; achieves highest recall/nDCG in broad mode, highest F1/F2 in core mode across 20 Cochrane reviews (585 ground-truth articles); user study: 78% preference over specialized tools (n=279 researchers, 18 countries)
comments: Rigorous multi-benchmark validation with novel trimodal retrieval and evidence-traceable design; strong real-world usability signals but limited in clinical trial application examples.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Hierarchical decomposition with multi-round verification and source grounding eliminates citation fabrication and preserves recall in systematic reviews

title: Assessment and good practices identification among NAPs of developing countries
task: Assessment and identification of good practices in National Adaptation Plans (NAPs) of developing countries
key_results: 60 NAPs reviewed; average content scores 75% of elements defining good NAP; NAP-Consistency scores higher than NAP-Coverage; strong factbase on vulnerabilities, weaker on M&E, participation, and finance
comments: Comprehensive global policy analysis with structured framework; identifies actionable gaps but lacks quantitative metrics linking NAP quality to climate resilience outcomes.

model_io.model: NAP-Good Practices Review Framework (NAP-Coverage and NAP-Consistency dimensions)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Current NAPs achieve ~75% content adequacy but lag on monitoring, participation, and financing mechanisms
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: average 75% content coverage; NAP-Consistency>NAP-Coverage; M&E/participation/finance identified as bottlenecks

title: Momentum-driven reversible logic accelerates efficient irreversible universal computation
task: Momentum-driven reversible logic for efficient universal computation using Josephson-junction parametrons
key_results: Erasure-Flip (EF) operation leveraging momentum achieves higher fidelity and faster computation than fixed-point Controlled Erasure (CE) without additional energetic cost; demonstrates universality via NAND gates
comments: Novel theoretical insight into momentum as computational resource; shows promise for superconducting logic but lacks experimental realization.

model_io.model: 2-bit logical unit: CE (fixed-point metastable) vs. EF (momentum-leveraging reversible+irreversible hybrid)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Momentum degree of freedom enables reversible logic to achieve universality and faster computation without energy overhead
hypotheses.result: Confirmed theoretically: EF outperforms CE in fidelity and speed; universality demonstrated via NAND
